$comment: Mission 1.84.19. The provider-strict projection of output schema v1.2.0 and everything said about it, re-derived by CI gate 92. The contract keeps deciding stage 5 locally; this projection is what a strict tool would carry, and nothing more.

DOCUMENTATION_FETCHES.note: Each page was read twice: once to review it, and once by the script that recorded the rows above. Both reads of each page gave the same SHA-256. E03 was requested at the path the platform's own pages link to and redirected to define-tools; the redirect is recorded.

STRICT_TOOL_USE_SUPPORTED.verbatim: * **Strict tool use** (`strict: true`): Guarantee schema validation on tool names and inputs

NO_BETA_HEADER.verbatim: beta headers are no longer required

STRICT_FLAG_LOCATION.verbatim: Set `"strict": true` as a top-level property in your tool definition, alongside `name`, `description`, and `input_schema`.

STRICT_TOOL_USE_GUARANTEES_INPUT_SCHEMA_.verbatim: While structured outputs guarantee schema compliance in most cases, there are scenarios where the output may not match your schema:

SUBSET_SHARED.verbatim: Structured outputs support standard JSON Schema with some limitations. Both JSON outputs and strict tool use share these limitations.

TYPES_SUPPORTED.verbatim: * All basic types: object, array, string, integer, number, boolean, null

ENUM_SUPPORTED.verbatim: * `enum` (strings, numbers, bools, or nulls only - no complex types

REQUIRED_AND_ADDITIONAL_PROPERTIES_FALSE.verbatim: * `required` and `additionalProperties` (must be set to `false` for objects)

UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE_IS_A_400.verbatim: If you use an unsupported feature, you'll receive a 400 error with details.

PATTERN_PARTIAL.verbatim: Simple regex patterns work well. Complex patterns may result in 400 errors.

SDK_DESCRIPTION_TRANSFORMATION.verbatim: 5. **Validate responses** against your original schema (with all constraints)

ENUM_CAPITALIZATION_NOT_GUARANTEED.verbatim: Structured outputs don't guarantee the capitalization of string `enum` and `const` values
This applies to both JSON outputs and strict tool use.

REFUSAL_AND_MAX_TOKENS_MAY_NOT_MATCH.verbatim: * The output may not match your schema because the refusal message takes precedence over schema constraints
* The output may be incomplete and not match your schema

COMPLEXITY_LIMITS.verbatim: you'll receive a 400 error with the message "Schema is too complex for compilation."

FIRST_REQUEST_COMPILATION_LATENCY.verbatim: * **First request latency:** The first time you use a specific schema, there is additional latency while the grammar compiles
* **Automatic caching:** Compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours from last use

INJECTED_FORMAT_PROMPT.verbatim: When using structured outputs, Claude automatically receives an additional system prompt explaining the expected output format.

SCHEMA_CACHED_24H.verbatim: Tool schemas are temporarily cached for up to 24 hours since last use. Prompts and responses are not retained beyond the API response.

FORCED_TOOL_USE_RESTRICTIONS.verbatim: Not every model and setting supports forced tool use.

FORCED_TOOL_USE_WITH_STRICT.verbatim: Note that when you have `tool_choice` as `any` or `tool`, the API prefills the assistant message to force a tool to be used.

OVERVIEW_STRICT.verbatim: Add `strict: true` to your custom tool definitions to ensure Claude's tool calls always match your schema exactly.

exceptions: a refusal (stop_reason refusal) may not match the schema
an output cut at max_tokens may not match the schema
the capitalization of enum and const values is not guaranteed

ADDITIONAL_PROPERTIES_FALSE_SUPPORTED.note: must be false for every object; any other value is not supported

STRING_MAX_LENGTH_SUPPORTED.note: minLength and maxLength are not supported; using one is a 400 error

ARRAY_MAX_ITEMS_SUPPORTED.note: only minItems of 0 or 1 is supported

PATTERN_SUPPORTED.note: anchors, *, +, ?, character classes, ., \d, \w, \s and groups are listed; simple {n,m} cases are supported and complex ones with large ranges are not, and neither is defined. A pattern carrying a counted quantifier is therefore not established as supported, and all three of the contract's patterns carry one

ENUM_SUPPORTED.note: string, number, boolean or null members; capitalization not guaranteed

STRICT_FLAG_LOCATION.note: beside name, description and input_schema, never inside input_schema

FORCED_TOOL_CHOICE_COMPATIBLE.note: forced tool_choice is restricted only under manual extended thinking and on Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1; claude-sonnet-5 with thinking disabled is neither, and the documentation describes combining forced tool choice with strict tool use

SYNCHRONOUS_MESSAGES_API_COMPATIBLE.note: strict is a property of a tool definition in a Messages API request; the documentation's examples use POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages

COMMERCIAL_TERMS_ROUTE.note: strict mode is a request property on the route the provider register already approves, not a new route, a new product or a new data flow

CAVEATS.handling: local stage 5 compares enum members exactly, so a case variant is refused
the completion is read from stop_reason before any parse, unchanged

the explicit limits hold (1 strict tool, 0 optional parameters, 0 union types); the internal grammar-size limits are undocumented, and a schema too complex to compile is a 400 error the one approved request would spend

the first request with a schema waits while its grammar compiles, for an undocumented time up to a 180-second compilation timeout; the 60-second request timeout is kept as frozen, so a long compilation would end the one call
the documentation says structured outputs add a system prompt explaining the format; its size is not documented and it is not in the request body the estimate measures
the projected schema is cached by the provider for up to 24 hours; it carries no TED value, no identifier and no subject, which this gate checks

A class C bound cannot be exceeded by a duplicate-free answer drawn from a rendered vocabulary; a class D bound sits on a value the model copies; a class B pattern fixes the canonical form of a copied identifier, which the descriptions sent unchanged describe in words and format uuid still constrains for the two id arrays. Local stage 5 enforces every one of them unchanged

DESCRIPTION_POLICY.why: the provider's SDKs can move removed constraints into descriptions; that is a client convenience, not an API requirement. Every removed bound on text the model composes is already stated in words by prompt v1.5.0, rendered from the same schema, so a description copy would be a second rendering of the same number. The contract's own descriptions are sent unchanged, and none is rewritten or weakened
